tests.mutation: LineOfSight.Combinations normalised row (1) into § 107.31(a)'s singular (`"(1) The remote pilot in command and the person manipulating the flight control of the small unmanned aircraft system; or"` for `"... the person manipulating the flight controls of the small unmanned aircraft system; or"`), so § 107.31(b)(1) stopped being quoted as the corpus prints it and the difference between the two paragraphs -- (a) "flight control", (b)(1) "flight controls" -- was smoothed away. This test went red alone with `Assert.Equal() Failure: Collections differ` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0).

VisualLineOfSightFinding.Authority cited the dependency's paragraph instead of this entry's section (`MapEntries.UnaidedVisualContact.Locator` for `MapEntries.VisualLineOfSight.Locator`), so § 107.31 as a whole was answered under § 107.31(a) and the two entries' findings stopped being tellable apart by their citations. This test went red with `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ`, together with the citation test and the dictionary-dispatch test (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with the caller's waiver statement replaced by one the engine made up (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

VisualLineOfSightFinding.ExercisedByTheRemotePilotInCommandAndThePersonManipulatingTheFlightControls read § 107.31(b)(1) as a disjunction of the two persons it names (`Exercise.RemotePilotInCommand || Exercise.PersonManipulatingTheFlightControls` for `&&`), so either one of them alone satisfied a row that says "The remote pilot in command **and** the person manipulating the flight controls". The four cases of the theory where exactly one of the two exercised the ability went red with `Assert.Equal() Failure: Values differ` (`Failed!  - Failed:     4, Passed:   312, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0).

VisualLineOfSightFinding.Maintained dropped the dependency's half (`Exercised` for `Ability.Holds && Exercised`), so § 107.31 came out maintained on an assertion that the aircraft could not be seen unaided at all -- (b) requires "the ability described in paragraph (a)" to be exercised, and there was no such ability. This test went red alone with `Assert.False() Failure` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0).

LineOfSight.Maintained caught the dependency's demand and invented an answer for it (the `UnaidedVision.SeenThroughoutTheFlight(waiver, assertions)` call wrapped in `try`/`catch (AssertionRequiredException)` yielding `Resolution<UnaidedVisualContactFinding>.FromValue(new UnaidedVisualContactFinding(new Assertion(MapEntries.UnaidedVisualContact, true, "remote pilot in command"), waiver))`), so a caller who asserted nothing -- or asserted under this entry's own id, which the map gives no assertedBy -- had § 107.31(a) answered yes on the engine's word. This test went red alone with `Assert.Throws() Failure: No exception was thrown` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0).

LineOfSight.Maintained demanded the dependency's assertion above its own gate (`var stated = Assertions.Stated(MapEntries.UnaidedVisualContact, assertions);` hoisted above the `Waivers.Suspension` check), so a caller stating a waiver of § 107.31 in force and asserting nothing -- which is the whole of the case -- was asked for a fact the waiver had made irrelevant instead of being told the entry is out of reach. This test went red alone with `FaaPart107.AssertionRequiredException : the map entry 'unaided-visual-contact' is an assertion; the caller must supply its value` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with the gate consulted against the dependency's entry rather than this one, which made the decline name unaided-visual-contact and § 107.31(a) (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

LineOfSight.Maintained handed the dependency a statement the engine made up rather than the caller's (`UnaidedVision.SeenThroughoutTheFlight(WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(Regulation, "the engine"), assertions)` for `(waiver, assertions)`), so the finding carried § 107.31 waived by nobody on the engine's own word and lost who was answerable for saying so -- the defect PRs #70 and #74 failed review for. This test went red with `Assert.Same() Failure: Values are not the same instance`, together with the two-rows test and the dictionary-dispatch test (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0).

Handlers.VisualLineOfSight defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(LineOfSight.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, request.EntryId, nameof(request.Waiver))`), so a caller who said nothing about § 107.205(c) had the engine say it for them -- and defaulting to "no waiver" convicts a holder. This test went red alone with `Assert.Throws() Failure: No exception was thrown` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with a missing exercise defaulted to a visual observer (`Failed!  - Failed:     2, Passed:   314, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

LineOfSight.Maintained compared the statement's regulation with itself (`Waivers.Suspension(MapEntries.VisualLineOfSight, waiver.Regulation, waiver)` for `(..., Regulation, waiver)`), so a stated waiver of § 107.33 suspended § 107.31 and the entry declined under a certificate that does not reach it. This test went red alone with `Assert.Throws() Failure: No exception was thrown` (`Failed!  - Failed:     1, Passed:   315, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with the gate consulted against the dependency's entry, which made the refusal name unaided-visual-contact (`Assert.Contains() Failure: Sub-string not found`, `Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

LineOfSight.Maintained consulted the gate against the dependency's entry instead of its own (`Waivers.Suspension(MapEntries.UnaidedVisualContact, Regulation, waiver)` for `Waivers.Suspension(MapEntries.VisualLineOfSight, Regulation, waiver)`), so this entry's decline became its dependency's word for word -- and since § 107.205(c) lists the whole of § 107.31 both declines already cite § 107.205 and carry OutsideCurrentScope, what was attempted is the only thing left that tells them apart. This test went red with `Assert.NotEqual() Failure: Strings are equal`, together with the waiver-in-force test and the wrong-regulation test (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with VisualLineOfSightFinding.Authority citing the dependency's § 107.31(a) (`Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

Handlers.VisualLineOfSight defaulted a missing exercise to a visual observer (`request.Exercise ?? new ExerciseOfTheAbility(false, false, true)` for `Demand(request.Exercise, request.EntryId, nameof(request.Exercise))`), so `Registry.Resolve(id, RuleRequest)` -- which builds the request from the assertions alone and can carry no exercise -- answered § 107.31 maintained under § 107.31(b)(2) instead of refusing, and the typed and untyped paths stopped behaving alike. This test went red with `Assert.Equal() Failure: Strings differ`, together with the refuses-rather-than-infer test (`Failed!  - Failed:     2, Passed:   314, Skipped:     0, Total:   316` on net8.0 and net10.0). It went red too with VisualLineOfSightFinding.Authority citing the dependency's § 107.31(a), and with the caller's waiver statement replaced by one the engine made up (each `Failed!  - Failed:     3, Passed:   313, Skipped:     0, Total:   316`).

`Handlers.VisualLineOfSight` demanded the typed input ahead of the rule's § 107.205 gate -- the ordering thirteen of the fifteen gated entries took before #93 -- by wrapping the argument back up (`Demand(request.Exercise, request.EntryId, nameof(request.Exercise))` for `request.Exercise`). A caller stating a certificate of waiver of § 107.31 in force and describing nothing else was then refused `ArgumentException` naming `Exercise` -- `FactRequired`, `MissingInput=Exercise`, filed under `Outstanding`, which `OperationEvaluation.Outstanding` documents as "everything the caller still owes this engine" -- instead of being declined `OutsideCurrentScope` citing § 107.205 (`docs/decisions/0008-the-waiver-gate-precedes-every-other-demand.md`). So this test, which pins one answer for a waived request, the same across every gated entry, went red on both target frameworks: `Failed!  - Failed:     4, Passed:   739, Skipped:     0, Total:   743` for net10.0 and the same figures for net8.0. The others red with it were `WaiverGateOrderingTests.A_waived_request_is_never_asked_for_a_typed_input_the_waiver_has_made_irrelevant`; `WaiverGateOrderingTests.Nothing_a_stated_waiver_suspends_is_reported_as_something_the_caller_still_owes`; `VisualLineOfSightEntryPointTests.The_dictionary_dispatch_answers_and_refuses_the_same_way`.
